details: Major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP, saw declines following the release of mixed U.S. manufacturing data. Bitcoin experienced rejection at the $87,000 resistance level, leading to over $190 million in crypto liquidations. Concurrently, the probability of an October Federal Reserve interest rate hike decreased to 18% after a weaker-than-expected September jobs report, with markets now pricing a 68.7% chance of a December hike.
title: Bitcoin Retreats Amid Macro Data, Fed Hike Odds Shift

details: The U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) announced the withdrawal of two proposed cryptocurrency regulations. These proposals, dating from 2023 and 2020, would have mandated banks to report transactions involving crypto mixers and to record and report larger transfers to self-hosted wallets, respectively. FinCEN cited concerns about a "chilling effect on legitimate activity" and excessive reporting burdens.
title: US Treasury Withdraws Crypto Mixer & Self-Hosted Wallet Rules

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has approved a rule change, permitting the Cboe BZX exchange to list six new funds from Volatility Shares. Among these are two funds designed to deliver three times the daily price movement of Bitcoin and Ether. These approved cryptocurrency funds will utilize futures contracts rather than holding direct digital assets, with trading expected to commence soon.
title: SEC Approves 3x Bitcoin and Ether Futures ETFs

details: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has taken an initial step towards establishing regulatory guidelines for leveraged cryptocurrency trading. This action signals a move towards creating a more defined and structured regulatory framework for this segment of the crypto market.
title: CFTC Initiates Leveraged Crypto Trading Rules Development
